data.title: Choose a skill, connector, plugin or cloud task
data.summary: Understand which layer supplies instructions, which supplies access and where the work actually runs.

facts.text: OpenAI plugins can bundle skills and MCP servers. Skills encode reusable instructions; MCP servers expose tools and data with their own authentication. Some plugins are desktop-only.
Claude plugins bundle skills and connectors. Remote connectors reach cloud services; desktop extensions supply local integrations and have different surface support.
Claude Code supports project, personal, plugin and account-synced skills with different distribution scopes. Do not assume one local skill appears in every host.

prerequisites: Identify the intended host, task, source data and existing access.
steps: Start with the task and inspect the host’s existing skills and installed plugins.
Use instructions for a repeatable process; choose a connector/MCP only when external data or actions are needed.
Check the supported host and execution environment before assuming local and cloud capabilities match.
Inspect the publisher, permissions, tools and any executable hooks before installing or enabling a bundle.
data.output: A short integration choice with host, data path, permissions and missing prerequisites.
validation: The chosen integration exists in the intended host and uses the expected external identity.
A Markdown instruction file is not presented as an installed connector.
limitations: This is a conceptual choice guide, not a certification of any plugin. Availability and workspace policy vary.
